title: HyDra: SOT-CAM Based Vector Symbolic Macro for Hyperdimensional Computing
problem: HDC accelerators suffer from high latency and energy costs in encoding, binding, permutation, and similarity search operations, limiting their practical deployment.
motivation: Energy-efficient HDC accelerators can enable scalable brain-inspired computing for edge and IoT applications.
method: HyDra accelerates hyperdimensional computing (a computation method using massive high-dimensional vectors) by performing critical operations directly in memory using SOT-MRAM, a fast and energy-efficient magnetic memory technology configured as a CAM—searchable memory that finds matching content rather than retrieving by fixed address. This architecture supports three key operations in-memory: binding (combining vectors through bitwise operations), permutation (rearranging bit order), and similarity search (measuring how closely vectors match). A bit-drop permutation method—which skips certain bit positions during rearrangement—reduces latency by 6x. Additional optimizations for addition operations and four-stage voltage scaling (which reduces power loss in interconnects) further decrease energy consumption and chip area.
key_novelty: HyDra pairs SOT-MRAM based CAM (searchable memory using magnetic storage) with a bit-drop permutation technique that rearranges bits more efficiently, achieving 6x speedup in hyperdimensional computing.
contributions: SOT-CAM integration for in-memory binding, permutation, and search
Bit-drop permutation method with 6x latency improvement
HDC-specific adder reducing energy and area by 1.51x and 1.43x
21.5x-552.74x energy reduction vs. CMOS implementations, 2.27x lower energy vs. state-of-the-art
limitations: SOT-MRAM variability and yield issues may impact practical deployment at scale.
